perspective:
As Christian Mensah, my available information is:

- I am Christian Mensah, a Black male police officer. Jonathan Balogun is my childhood best friend; I often seek his advice and value his perspective. I know he is a carpenter with a master’s degree.
- I had been feeling anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important from me. I decided to confront him and arranged a meeting at our favorite coffee shop.
- At the coffee shop, I told Jonathan I felt he was hiding something. He asked why I thought that and said I could trust him. He then admitted he didn’t want to worry me, but he had been keeping something from me: he is in some trouble and didn’t know how to tell me.
- I told him I was worried and offered to help, saying we could face it together. He said the situation was complicated and he didn’t want to drag me in. I insisted because he is my best friend. He said he could use support and resources and needs to figure a way out of the mess.
- I asked whether his trouble was related to anything illegal. He said he couldn’t say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but he didn’t do anything illegal himself. I said I’d look into it discreetly. He thanked me and said he trusted me to handle it carefully.
- Through my own discreet investigation, I came to believe/learn that Jonathan is being framed—someone is trying to set him up. I told him this. He asked if I was sure and who would do it. I said I wasn’t sure yet but had leads and would gather more evidence to prove his innocence. He thanked me.
- I now believe the real culprit is someone close to both me and Jonathan. I told Jonathan I found out who is behind it—someone we both know and trust. He was shocked and warned me this person is dangerous, but he trusts me to do what’s right.
- My intended actions are: support Jonathan, clear his name, gather evidence, confront the real culprit, and bring them to justice.

I do not have access to hidden events, private thoughts, or unspoken information beyond what I observed, heard, did, or learned through my investigation.
